name: @pixfrix/search-console-mcp

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists every Search Console property the connected Google account can read, with its type and permission level. Call this first when you do not know the exact property name.

tools.name: search_analytics
tools.description: Runs a raw Search Console performance query: clicks, impressions, CTR and average position, broken down by any mix of query, page, country, device, date, hour and search appearance, with filters. Use it for anything the specialised tools do not cover. Rows come back sorted by clicks unless order_by says otherwise.

site_url.description: Search Console property, for example "sc-domain:example.com" or "https://www.example.com/". A bare domain or any page URL on the site also works. Optional when GSC_SITE_URL is set or the account has exactly one property.

start_date.description: First day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific Time. Defaults to `days` before end_date.

end_date.description: Last day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific Time, or "today" / "yesterday". Defaults to the latest day Google has complete data for, usually 3 to 4 days ago. A later date includes days that are still incomplete.

days.description: Length of the period in days, used when start_date is not given. Default 28.

dimensions.description: How to break the numbers down, in order. Empty returns one row of totals. "searchAppearance" cannot be combined with other dimensions. "hour" needs data_state "hourly_all" and only covers the last few days.

filters.description: Filters; a row must match all of them. Example: [{"dimension":"page","operator":"contains","expression":"/blog/"},{"dimension":"country","operator":"equals","expression":"usa"}]. Countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, devices are DESKTOP, MOBILE or TABLET, and the regex operators use RE2 syntax.

search_type.description: Which Google surface: web (default), image, video, news (the News tab), discover or googleNews.

data_state.description: "all" (default) matches the Search Console website: complete days, plus partial numbers for recent days if the period reaches that far. "final" leaves out any day that is not final yet. "hourly_all" is for the hour dimension.

aggregation_type.description: How impressions are counted: "byProperty" counts a search once however many of your pages appear, "byPage" counts each page. Leave unset for Google's default.

order_by.description: Sort by this metric instead of clicks. The tool then reads up to 25,000 rows and sorts them locally, so "top by impressions" is correct within that scan.

order.description: Sort direction. Default desc, or asc for position (best first).

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return.

start_row.description: Zero-based offset, for paging through results.

tools.name: find_quick_wins
tools.description: Finds "striking distance" keywords: queries where a page already ranks just below the top results (positions 4 to 20 by default) and is being seen. These are the cheapest rankings to improve. Returns each query with its page and an estimate of the extra clicks from reaching the target position, plus the pages with the most combined potential.

tools.name: inspect_url
tools.description: Asks Google how it sees one URL: whether it is indexed and why not, the canonical Google chose against the declared one, when it was last crawled and as which device, robots.txt and noindex state, the sitemaps and pages that point to it, and structured data problems. It reports the indexed version, not a live test. Counts against a quota of 2,000 inspections per day per property.

tools.name: inspect_urls
tools.description: Runs URL inspection for up to 50 URLs of one property and returns a compact table of which are indexed, their coverage state, last crawl and the problems found. Each URL uses one of the 2,000 daily inspections per property.

tools.name: audit_sitemap_indexing
tools.description: Reads the URLs listed in the property's sitemaps, inspects a sample of them and reports how many are indexed, the reasons the others are not, and the affected URLs. This is the closest the API gets to the Page indexing report. Each inspected URL uses one of the 2,000 daily inspections per property, so the sample is small by default.

site_url.description: Search Console property, for example "sc-domain:example.com" or "https://www.example.com/". A bare domain or any page URL on the site also works. Optional when GSC_SITE_URL is set or the account has exactly one property.

max_urls.description: How many URLs to inspect. Google takes about six seconds per inspection, so 25 takes around 25 seconds and 50 is the most one call can finish. Call again for a second sample.

instructions:
Google Search Console data and SEO analysis for the properties the connected Google account can read.

Getting started: call list_sites if you do not know the property. Every tool accepts site_url as an exact property name, a bare domain or any page URL on the site.

Choosing a tool: get_performance_overview for the big picture; compare_periods, find_declining_pages and detect_traffic_anomalies to explain change; find_quick_wins, find_ctr_opportunities, find_keyword_cannibalization and find_content_gaps to find work worth doing; analyze_page before editing a page; inspect_url, inspect_urls and audit_sitemap_indexing for indexing questions; search_analytics for any custom query.

Reading the data:
- Dates are in Pacific Time. Without dates, tools use the 28 days ending on the latest day Google has complete data for (usually 3 to 4 days ago). end_date accepts "today" and "yesterday"; a period that reaches past the last complete day returns partial numbers for those days and says so.
- position is the average topmost position; lower is better.
- ctr_pct values are percentages (3.2 means 3.2%).
- Rows broken down by query exclude anonymised queries, so they sum to less than the totals.
- Results are JSON. Tables are {"columns": [...], "rows": [[...], ...]}.
- URL inspection is limited to 2,000 calls per day per property; prefer the sampling tools over inspecting everything.
